7698054304732695815.title: 3 seconds. That's all that stood between Lemi Berhanu and the Amsterdam course record this morning. Berhanu won the 2026 TCS Amsterdam Marathon in 2:03:33 - three seconds shy of the 2:03:30 record - leading a Kenyan 2-3 from Nicholas Kipkorir (2:03:39) and Patrick Mosin (2:03:58). Defending champion Kipchumba, Alew, and Getachew never made the podium. The women's race delivered the record the men couldn't: Buze Diriba smashed the course record to win in 2:16:12, ahead of Aynalem Desta (2:17:06). #marathonwinner #amsterdammarathon #runners

7698297658057755911.title: Yesterday's fastest marathon wasn't in Amsterdam. Tamirat Tola won the Beijing Marathon this morning in 2:03:10, a course record by nearly four minutes and the fastest marathon ever run on Chinese roads. Ethiopian sweep behind him: Muktar Edris 2:04:34, Adane Kebede Gebre 2:05:10. All three under the old record. Women: Anchinalu Dessie defended in 2:20:36. The twist: Lemi Berhanu, Beijing's two-time defending champion, chose Amsterdam instead. His 2:03:33 there was 23 seconds slower than Tola. #beijingmarathon2026 #marathonresults #ethiopianrunning #roadracing #runningculture

7698791199695473928.title: Most runners don't lose fitness on hard days. They lose it on easy days that quietly turned hard. Five mistakes that kill your easy runs: running them too fast, chasing the watch, racing your friends, cramming in a missed workout, and thinking slow is pointless. Rule of thumb: easy pace is 60-90 s/km slower than your 5K pace, and about 80% of your weekly running should feel like it. Save this for your next easy run, and follow for more training explained. #easyrun #zone2running #8020running #runningmistakes #aerobicbase
